newsitem.title: USA: Primark sees earnings lower than estimates.
newsitem.headline: Primark sees earnings lower than estimates.

text.p: Information services company Primark Corp. stock fell 22 percent Thursday after it said its first quarter earnings per share will be lower than analysts expected.

Primark said earnings would likely be about 10 cents below the 25 cents consensus among industry analysts compiled by First Call. In last year's first quarter, Primark earned $6.4 million, or 24 cents a share.
"It is not anticipated that this first quarter shortfall will be recovered over the balance of the year," the company said in a statement.
Shares of Primark were down $5.25 to $18.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Primark blamed foreign currency movements and continuing operating problems at Groupe DAFSA, its Paris-based information business, and TIMCO, its aircraft maintenance subsidiary for the decline.

The company, which provides software and electronic databases to financial markets, governments, and computer firms around the world, said it has assigned a top executive to tackle the Groupe DAFSA problems and bring it to "an acceptable level of performance by the second half of the year."
